diagnostic_evidence.quote: On the other hand, for $n_0=0.25$, the policy related to $\J^2$ performs poorly since the mean TTP has more than halved if compared to the other treatment approaches.

issues.failure_explanation: The introduction asserts that with the hyperbolic cost the computed policy 'on average outperforms MTD and AT' in time-to-progression. The paper's own results contradict this for n_0=0.25: the hyperbolic policy's mean TTP is 102 days versus 210 (MTD) and 213 ('On-Off' AT) days, a more-than-halving that the body itself labels as the policy performing 'poorly'. The outperformance holds only for n_0=0.5 (336 vs 270/285 days) and n_0=0.75 (660 vs 410/462 days); no defined aggregation over the three different initial tumor sizes would make the unqualified claim accurate.

failure_location.quote: However, when $\ell$ has a hyperbolic profile, the computed policy suggests a delayed starting of the therapy, and on average it outperforms MTD and AT in terms of `time to progression' (see \cref{table:MTD_AT1,table:Sum_Hyp}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the sentence to the regimes where it holds, e.g. state that for n_0=0.5 and n_0=0.75 the hyperbolic policy improves the mean TTP over MTD and 'On-Off' AT, while for n_0=0.25 the mean TTP more than halves, matching the body's own discussion.
issues.overall_effect: The introductory summary materially overstates the hyperbolic-cost strategy's performance; a reader relying on it would miss that for n_0=0.25 the mean TTP more than halves. The accurate, qualified statement already appears in the results section; no theorem, lemma, or algorithm is affected.
issues.title: Introduction overclaims that the hyperbolic-cost policy outperforms MTD and AT on average
issues.why_classification: A one-sentence qualification in the introduction aligns the claim with the paper's own tables and discussion; every substantive result, table, and guarantee is unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Regarding the parameter $\hat f_0$, we divided the interval $[0.002,1]$ into $49$ nodes with a constant step equal to $0.002$.
which has a support consisting of $N=1225$ points.

issues.failure_explanation: With spacing 0.02, the set {0.5, 0.52, ..., 1} contains 26 points, not 25; with spacing 0.002, the set {0.002, 0.004, ..., 0.1} contains 50 points, not 49 (the written interval [0.002,1] is itself a misprint of [0.002,0.1]). Hence the support Theta_N in eq:Theta_N_simul has 26x50=1300 points, not N=1225, and the measure mu_N in eq:mu_N_simul (weights 1/25 and 1/49 over 25x49 atoms) has neither support Theta_N nor total mass one (mass 2600/1225), so as written it is not a probability measure as required to apply thm:exist_Gamma. The correction is not unique (keep 25/49 atoms and drop an endpoint from each grid, or use 26/50 nodes with weights 1/26 and 1/50), so this is a genuine inconsistency rather than a typo.

failure_location.quote: In our specific setting, we discretized the interval $[0.5,1]$ where $\hat r_R$ varies into $25$ equi\-spaced nodes with distance $0.02$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the grid description consistent: either use 26 nodes in [0.5,1] and 50 nodes in [0.002,0.1] with weights 1/26 and 1/50 and N=1300, or keep 25/49 nodes with weights 1/25 and 1/49 by removing one endpoint from each grid, and renormalize mu_N to a probability measure on Theta_N.
issues.overall_effect: The ensemble cardinality and quadrature weights behind every numerical experiment (the minimizations of J^1 and J^2 and all mean TTPs over Theta_N) are misstated, and the stated mu_N violates the standing hypothesis mu_N in P(Theta) needed to invoke thm:exist_Gamma. Because the objective changes only by a constant rescaling and the TTP means are uniform averages, no reported numerical conclusion changes once the counts are corrected.
issues.title: Ensemble grid miscounted: stated node numbers, support size N=1225, and weights 1/25, 1/49 are mutually inconsistent
issues.why_classification: A contained counting and renormalization fix restores full consistency; the optimization problems, the discrete functionals, and all reported TTP statistics survive unchanged, so no mathematical content is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The mean TTP is computed by taking the average over the elements of the set $\Theta_N$

issues.failure_explanation: For n_0=0.75 the simulation horizon is T_hor=1500 days (table:Time_horizon), and the reported max TTP of 'Off-On' AT is exactly 1500 days (table:Off-On). Since TTP' (eq:def_TTP') is computed as the supremum of the below-threshold times over the simulated window, a value exactly equal to the horizon endpoint means at least one tumor had not progressed by the end of the simulation, so its true TTP' is unknown (greater than 1500). The censored value is reported as exact and enters both the max and the mean TTP (589 days, against 462 for 'On-Off' AT), making the claimed improvement for n_0=0.75 - the largest in the table - unreliable as reported; the caption neither discloses the censoring nor states which of TTP/TTP' was used for 'Off-On' AT.

failure_location.quote: The outcomes of `Off-On'~AT seem promising, as it shows an improvement in almost every performance indicator compared to `Off-On'~AT.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the 'Off-On' AT trajectories with a horizon that exceeds its own best TTP (as was done when calibrating the horizon for 'On-Off' AT), or treat horizon-censored values explicitly (report them as censored and use a censoring-aware statistic); at minimum, disclose that max TTP = 1500 days corresponds to tumors that had not progressed by the end of the simulation window.
issues.overall_effect: The n_0=0.75 row of table:Off-On and the accompanying claim that 'Off-On' AT improves almost every performance indicator are unreliable: censored-at-horizon values are averaged in as if exact, plausibly inflating the reported mean (589 vs 462 days) and max (1500 vs 1196 days). The endorsement of 'Off-On' AT in the Final considerations inherits the caveat. No formal theorem is affected.
issues.title: 'Off-On' AT TTPs for n_0=0.75 are censored at the 1500-day simulation horizon but reported as exact
issues.why_classification: The defect is confined to the numerical reporting for one strategy at n_0=0.75 and admits a contained repair (a longer-horizon re-simulation or censoring-aware statistics, with no new proof architecture), but the source as written cannot certify the headline numbers, which may be materially inflated by censored values.
